name: Federal income tax, CPP/QPP, EI and QPIP parameters, 2026
name_fr: Impôt fédéral sur le revenu et cotisations sociales, 2026
description: Federal personal income tax brackets and credits for the 2026 tax year, plus the employee payroll contributions that apply in every province (CPP or, in Quebec, QPP; Employment Insurance; and Quebec's QPIP). Provincial and territorial tax is added on top; see the nat-<prov>-income-and-sales-tax-2026 records.

attributes.legal_status: in force for 2026 payroll; CRA's January 2026 T4127 states that some income tax changes are applied 'if enacted as proposed' — the enactment status of the 14% lowest rate was not checked in this pass
attributes.residency_rule: Provincial/territorial tax is set by the province or territory of residence on 31 December 2026 (CRA current-year page).

cpp.tax_treatment: base portion (4.95/5.95 of the contribution) earns a non-refundable credit; the first additional portion and CPP2 are deductions from income

qpp_quebec.note: QPP maximum pensionable earnings equal the YMPE (74,600) as implied by the maximum contribution; the QPP second-additional ceiling was not separately confirmed

attributes.scheduled_change: CRA's July 2026 T4127 states the CPP base rate falls to 4.75% for employees and employers effective 1 January 2027.

sources.title: T4127 Payroll Deductions Formulas, 122nd edition, effective 1 January 2026 (Table 8.1 rates and thresholds; basic personal amounts; CPP/QPP/EI/QPIP parameters)
Current year tax rates and income brackets (2026) — page modified 2026-06-25
T4127 Payroll Deductions Formulas, 123rd edition, effective 1 July 2026 (mid-year changes: BC, PE, NL)
T4032-QC Payroll Deductions Tables, January 2026, general information (Quebec abatement 16.5%, Quebec EI rate)

verification.notes: Federal brackets agree between the CRA current-year page and T4127 Table 8.1. Payroll figures read from T4127 (Jan 2026); EI maximum insurable earnings stated in the second half of that document.

limitations: Employee side only; employer contributions not listed. Self-employed people pay both halves of CPP/QPP and are outside EI unless they opt in.
